title: Logspace computability of index deletion
statement: For a bit string $z$, parse it as an encoded pair $(u,b')$; then parse $u$ as an encoded pair $(w,b'')$ and return the encoding of $(w,b')$. If either parse fails, return the empty string. This resulting function is implicitly logspace computable: its output length is bounded by $C(|x|+1)^c$ for some natural numbers $C,c$ on every input $x$, and both the language of encoded pairs $(x,	ext{bits}(i))$ for which output bit $i$ is $1$ and the language of such pairs for which $i$ is less than the output length are decidable in logarithmic space.
